content.text:
**Recent major news for Bun, the fast all-in-one JavaScript runtime, package manager, test runner, and bundler (designed as a Node.js drop-in replacement using JavaScriptCore), centers on the release of Bun v1.4 in August 2026.**[[1]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)

### Key Highlights from Bun v1.4 (August 20, 2026)
- **Core rewrite from Zig to Rust**: The entire codebase (~780,000–1 million lines) was ported in just 11 days using ~64 parallel Claude AI agents (at ~$165K API cost), landing over 6,700 commits. The goal was to systematically eliminate entire classes of memory bugs at compile time. Benchmarks show the new version matches or beats v1.3 performance, with a ~20% smaller binary.[[2]](https://appwrite.io/blog/post/announcing-bun-1-4-runtime)
- **Significant performance and efficiency gains**:
  - Idle CPU usage reduced by up to 5x.
  - Memory usage cut by up to 35–48% (e.g., Fastify HTTP server from 233 MB to 120 MB; Express from 169 MB to 92 MB).
  - Startup 50% faster on Linux (hello-world from ~10.9 ms to 5.1 ms) and 2.5x faster on Windows.
  - Production wins reported in tools like Claude Code (p99 CPU from 24% to 10%).[[3]](https://scrydon.com/insights/2026/08/21/bun-1-4-at-scrydon/)
- **Node.js compatibility leap**: Passes +1,517 more tests from the Node.js test suite (biggest jump since v1.0). Now reports as Node.js 26-compatible. Many packages now work out-of-the-box, including Playwright, Next.js 16, Vitest, OpenTelemetry, Nuxt, and testcontainers. High test-pass rates for core modules like `node:http`, `node:fs`, `node:stream`, etc.[[4]](https://daily.dev/posts/bun-1-4-nz2dmgftt)
- **New built-in APIs and features** (replacing many external packages):
  - `Bun.Image` (faster than Sharp).
  - `Bun.WebView` (headless browser automation; uses system WebKit on macOS or drives Chrome/Chromium/Edge via CDP—no Puppeteer/Playwright needed).
  - `Bun.markdown`, `Bun.cron()`, `Bun.Terminal` (PTY support).
  - Native `ReadableStream`/`WritableStream`/`TransformStream`, `CompressionStream`/`DecompressionStream`.
  - ~3x faster `bun:ffi`.
  - Experimental HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 support in `Bun.serve()` and `fetch()`.
  - CLI improvements: `bun run --parallel`, `bun test --parallel`, `bun audit fix`, `bun dedupe`, `bun prune`, directory serving, Range/conditional requests, Windows on ARM64, and React Compiler integration in `bun build` (~20x faster than Babel plugin).[[5]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i38DgEuaJwM)
- **Over 2,900 GitHub issues fixed** since v1.3.[[6]](https://juejin.cn/post/7676105145394200610)

The release is available now (`bun upgrade` or via the install script). Canary builds (including early 1.4.0 versions) have been rolling out since late August 2026.[[7]](https://libraries.io/npm/bun)

### Background Context
- **Acquisition by Anthropic** (announced December 2025): Bun joined Anthropic to power Claude Code and the Claude Agent SDK. It remains fully open-source under the MIT license, with accelerated development. Bun has grown to over 20 million monthly downloads. Claude Code itself reached $1B run-rate revenue shortly before the acquisition.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bun_(software))
- The Rust rewrite was previewed in canary form earlier in 2026 and sparked some community debate around AI-assisted development, project maturity, open PRs, and memory/stability concerns in prior versions. However, v1.4 has seen positive early production results (e.g., on platforms like Appwrite and in services reporting 50%+ CPU/memory drops).[[9]](https://daily.dev/posts/bun-1-4-finally-ships-the-rust-rewrite-drama-isn-t-over--fdy7op2yl)

### Official Resources
- Full release notes: [bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)[[1]](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.4)
- Main site: [bun.com](https://bun.com/)
- GitHub: [github.com/oven-sh/bun](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun)
- Wikipedia entry (updated post-release): Stable release listed around v1.3.14 prior to 1.4.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bun_(software))

Bun continues to position itself as a batteries-included, high-performance alternative for full-stack JavaScript/TypeScript development, with strong momentum in 2026. For the absolute latest, check the official blog or GitHub releases.
